title: MERKLE TREES
subtitle: A tree of hashes: compare or verify huge datasets by looking at a handful of hashes.
footer: System Design, Step by Step · core concepts

blocks.text: Hash each block, hash pairs upwards to one root. One changed byte changes only the hashes on its path to the root.
Compare roots, skip every matching subtree, descend into mismatches. ~40 hashes find 1 bad range among a million.
Block + one sibling hash per level (~20 for 1M blocks) recomputes the root; match the trusted root and it's genuine.

items: Bitcoin light wallets, ZFS checksums, BitTorrent v2, IPFS
Trees must track writes, or be rebuilt before comparing (heavy I/O)
Leaves cover ranges: one changed key flags its whole range
Hash leaves and internal nodes differently (0x00 / 0x01)

blocks.text: "Besides read repair, replicas run anti-entropy with Merkle trees per key range: they compare root hashes and walk down only the branches that differ, exchanging a few dozen hashes instead of scanning a billion keys."
